idiom_name: AsyncSequence for-await pull (+ AsyncStream init(unfolding:)) with task cancellation
implementation_notes: Swift's structured concurrency replaces the polling loop with an async sequence: iterating for await message in channel - or driving an AsyncSequence's iterator directly - makes 'pull when ready' the next suspension point of the consuming task, AsyncStream's init(unfolding:) is the documented bridge for a genuinely pull-based source, and task cancellation is the shutdown path. A hand-written loop with an explicit sleep remains appropriate when the underlying client is poll-based and the batch bound and idle interval are part of the contract.
pitfalls: Cancellation is cooperative: it has no effect unless something checks it, so a consumer that never suspends or checks Task.isCancelled ignores shutdown entirely.

AsyncStream buffers by default (unbounded unless a buffering policy is given), so a fast producer and a slow consumer grow memory silently; .bufferingNewest/.bufferingOldest makes the backpressure explicit.
